body_markdown:
Listen, we get it. If you’re clicking on a story about a third-generation Chevrolet El Camino, you’re probably at least somewhat curious to see what’s beneath the hood. Is it a 396? Maybe the 454? Someone said this thing was rowdy, so surely it’s gonna make a lumpy noise, right?


Right? Somebody?


Well, maybe have a seat. This 1971 Chevrolet El Camino,[currently available on Hagerty Marketplace](https://www.hagerty.com/marketplace/auction/1971-Chevrolet-El-Camino/00f3af47-ab40-4701-9f4a-3298c03cb9fa) , doesn’t have an eight-cylinder engine at all. In fact, the engine doesn’t even hail from these shores. But that doesn’t make a lick of difference as to our intrigue with the machine.


Hagerty Marketplace | Jags-for-me


Instead, this ’71 El’ Co’ houses a *Toyota* engine—specifically, the vaunted 2JZ-GTE VVT-i inline-six engine that rocketed to fame beneath the hood of one of today’s hottest collector vehicles: the[Mk IV Toyota Supra](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/toyota/supra/1998/1998-toyota-supra-mk_iv_turbo?id=aCn1I000000CyhlSAC) .


Hagerty Marketplace | Jags-for-me


Before you get the pitchforks out, consider this: Aren’t enthusiast cars simply canvases on which their owners paint self-portraits? If someone’s going to delve into the vast and unending world of “going beyond stock,” are we obligated to slap imaginary guardrails in place, or is it better to let creative minds run wild?


Hagerty Marketplace | Jags-for-me


Your author would argue the latter—custom cars are an endless sandbox. While convention might dictate one thing, plenty of moments throughout the history of this hobby have been written by those who eschewed the expected for something that took it a step further. Imagine hearing someone lament the arrival of the[Hirohata Mercury](https://www.hagerty.com/media/video/legendary-hirohata-merc-shines-in-historic-vehicle-association-video-series/) , one of the founding icons of the custom-car movement?


Hagerty Marketplace | Jags-for-me


We’re not going as far as to compare a[Supra](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/smithology/smithology-secrets-of-the-supra-that-broke-actually-wore-out-the-mold/) -swapped El Camino to the[Hirohata Merc](https://www.hagerty.com/media/video/how-barris-kustoms-built-the-hirohata-mercury-in-only-14-days/) , but the same theory applies: Convention may argue for one thing, but bucking that notion can produce something plenty worthy of focused discussion.


Hagerty Marketplace | Jags-for-me


What’s more, this car is quite well done, from where we stand. The 2JZ-GTE VVT-i has been extensively modified, according to the listing. In place of the traditional twin-turbo setup that came stock on these, this example features a Precision 6766 single-blower setup (with a kickin’ pink inlet horn, we might add). That’s just the start, too; the listing notes a Royal Chamber intake manifold, ID1000 fuel injectors, and a Fuelab pressure regulator, an EFI fuel system with a 450-lph fuel pump, and tons more.


Hagerty Marketplace | Jags-for-me


Originally built by[XAT Racing](https://xatracing.com/?srsltid=AfmBOooqeRMuuSsEn34cXy3HXeC0e85iOrAcTue0ClkEykjJTycM4snH) for the All Supra Show, the listing says this[El Camino](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/the-original-hybrid-chevrolets-half-car-half-truck-is-just-right-for-collectors/) has been featured across numerous publications. We don’t doubt that one bit—such a wild blend of American style and Japanese engineering is well-deserving of a highlight.


Hagerty Marketplace | Jags-for-me


The listing does note a few rust bubbles and generous cosmetic imperfections to the House of Kolors Burgundy Wine custom paint, but we’d reckon those blemishes would be pretty tricky to spot as you dumped the clutch at full boost and laid waste to pretty much anything alongside you on the drag strip.


Hagerty Marketplace | Jags-for-me


We’re as big a fan of a big-block rumble as anyone on the site, but we’re also not opposed to alternative blends done well—and this ’71 El Caminco falls decidedly into that latter camp. It may not be for you, but it would be hard to meet a machine like this with total indifference.


Heck, the only thing harder might be beating this machine at your local drag night.
